case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed denial of the mother's motion to dismiss, holding the dismissal sanction for an untimely CHINS fact-finding hearing cannot be used to collaterally attack an adjudication already entered.
key_cases.relevance: Defines the point after which the statutory dismissal remedy is no longer available to a parent.
key_cases.quote: The dismissal sanction of Indiana Code Section 31-34-11-1(d) for failure to timely conduct a CHINS factfinding hearing is not a mechanism to collaterally attack a CHINS adjudication.

key_cases.holding: The court reversed the CHINS finding because the parents had cooperated fully and voluntarily obtained services, so there was insufficient evidence that the court's coercive intervention was necessary, noting an informal adjustment was available instead.
key_cases.relevance: Reversal of the CHINS finding requires dismissal where the coercion element fails.
key_cases.quote: There is insufficient evidence that the coercive intervention of a court is necessary to protect E.K.

key_cases.holding: The court reversed the CHINS adjudication because the Department failed to prove by a preponderance of the evidence the third statutory element, that the children needed care the parents were unlikely to provide without the court's coercive intervention.
key_cases.relevance: Failure of proof on any element requires dismissal of the CHINS petition.
key_cases.quote: To prove a child is “in need of services”, the Department must prove three statutory elements by a preponderance of the evidence

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed the placement of the child with his out-of-state father and the dismissal of the CHINS case, holding DCS's reunification efforts were reasonable and did not violate the statutory reasonable-efforts provision.
key_cases.relevance: Upholds dismissal of the CHINS case once the child was safely placed.
key_cases.quote: In light of the circumstances, we believe DCS's reunification efforts were reasonable.

key_cases.holding: The court held that because DCS failed to prove the statutory waiting-period element it alleged, the trial court was required to dismiss the termination petitions, and it reversed the terminations.
key_cases.quote: requiring a termination petition to allege four defined elements and commanding dismissal when DCS fails to prove each element by clear and convincing evidence
